_comment: COUPLING tier-2. deal.II's sides-table row: unstarred yes in both columns, 'coupled to FEniCSx and DUNE-fem, both roles'. deal.II is the only participant that does not exist until it is built — its payload says 'THE PARTICIPANT IS TWO FILES: a compiled C++ solver and a thin Python wrapper', ships heat_iface_dealii.cc and a CMakeLists next to the script, and gives the cmake invocation. So this fixture BUILDS the shipped source before coupling anything: if it does not compile against this install's deal.II, the claim that a deal.II participant is available here is false and the fixture says so instead of skipping. The payload's silent-wrong warning is specific — 'THE NODAL FLUX MUST BE AVERAGED OVER BOTH ADJACENT CELLS ... last-writer-wins silently biases every interior interface node toward one cell' — and a biased nodal flux still converges, showing up only as an interface flux off by a factor related to the cell size, which the closed-form comparison catches and a convergence check does not.
